why: Six drawings outside every icon, each ending its tag's name on a different character Angular's lexer ends a name on (`isNameEnd`): a `>`, a `/`, a tab, U+001F — a control character the lexer takes for whitespace and `\s` does not — a no-break space and an `=` (`<svg="1">`, an attribute with no name, which `ngc` compiles). The walk reads six drawings, and a count that ends a name on fewer characters than the lexer misses one: point 1 fires instead of point 2. Counted up to `[\s/>]`, the control character and the `=` were drawings to the walk alone, and beside an ICU's `<svg>` the two counts agreed.
